name: Anti-reflective interference coating
process: Thin metal-oxide layers are built up on both outer faces (SCHOTT applies them by a dip-coating process and burns the layers in), so the reflections from the layer boundaries interfere and cancel across the visible. The residual reflection is about an eighth of plain glass's, faintly coloured, and the coated faces are hard. Laid over low-iron glass for vitrines, where the visitor should see the object and not the room.
